Stream interrupted.\nOpen your PC’s app list to resume.

Native streams at this screen’s resolution and refresh rate with every latency setting on.
Smooth TV uses the same resolution and refresh rate, paced for the smoothest motion.
Wi-Fi / Away streams at two thirds of that resolution at 60 fps, for a weaker network.
Battery saver keeps that resolution at 30 fps.
PC profiles still take priority.

Lowest latency shows each frame at once; Balanced and Smoothest video wait for the screen’s refresh for steadier motion at more delay, keeping every frame adds more, and PC’s frame times shows each frame when the game drew it, a few milliseconds later. Where the PC times frames to your screen, Balanced shows one frame per refresh with an even picture when the stream matches the screen, for about one refresh more delay than Lowest latency (25 against 17 ms at 120 Hz); choose it when motion judders at the screen’s own rate, and Lowest latency for the least delay.

Off hides the overlay. Compact shows one line: rendered FPS, network round trip (RTT) and frame loss, behind a dot that turns amber or red when the stream struggles. Statistics shows live stream measurements. Debug adds timing percentiles and decoder diagnostics; scroll to see all details. You can also change it from the Control Center.

Learn how to wake a sleeping PC from the app.
Wakes a sleeping PC from this device. The PC needs Wake-on-LAN turned on and a wired network connection, and this device must have connected to it once while it was awake.
